title: Constant sheaves and constant complexes
statement:
For a scheme $T$, a commutative ring $\Lambda$ and a
$\Lambda$-module $M$, the *constant sheaf* $\underline{M}$ on
$T_{\Et}$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf
$U\mapsto M$ on the small etale site
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; it is the sheaf
of $M$-valued functions associated with the locally constant sheaf
with value $M$. For a complex $\mathcal M^\bullet$ of
$\Lambda$-modules, $\underline{\mathcal M^\bullet}$ is the termwise
constant complex of sheaves, and the operations are compatible with
shifts and with quasi-isomorphisms in $\mathcal M^\bullet$.

proof.text: Use the constant-sheaf construction [def-constructible-constant] with values in $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Its value at $M$ is precisely the sheafification of the presheaf with value $M$ and identity restrictions. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-locally-constant], this sheaf has the natural model $U\mapsto\operatorname{LocallyConstant}(|U|,M)$, with coefficient maps acting by postcomposition. Thus the function description means locally constant functions, with $M$ discrete, and does not require connectedness or finiteness.

source.place: first two sentences; Sites Example 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; Etale Cohomology Remark 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps

proof.text: Write $c$ for the constant-presheaf functor and $a$ for module sheafification. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], presheaf finite limits and finite colimits are computed sectionwise and $a$ is exact. For every object $U$, evaluation of $c$ is the identity functor on modules, so the kernel and cokernel of $c(f)$ are respectively $c(\ker f)$ and $c(\operatorname{coker}f)$, with identity restrictions. Also $c(f+g)=c(f)+c(g)$ sectionwise. Since $a$ preserves finite products and coproducts, it preserves their common biproduct structure: the diagonal, codiagonal, projections and injections. Writing $f+g$ as the diagonal followed by $f\oplus g$ followed by the codiagonal shows $a(f+g)=a(f)+a(g)$. Consequently $ac$ is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits. This proves exactness for arbitrary $\Lambda$ and arbitrary modules; the finite-ring and finite-module lemma is not needed.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact, first sentence of proof; Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact; Tag 03CS, section-presheaves-modules

proof.text: For a cochain complex $\mathcal M^\bullet$, define its constant complex by $(\underline{\mathcal M^\bullet})^r=ac(\mathcal M^r)$ and differential $ac(d^r)$; for a chain map use $ac$ in each degree. Functoriality and additivity give $ac(d^{r+1})ac(d^r)=ac(0)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact functor $ac$ from step 2: its termwise functor carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and has the natural shift isomorphism with identity degree components. Explicitly both $ac(\mathcal M[n])$ and $ac(\mathcal M)[n]$ have term $ac(\mathcal M^{r+n})$ and differential $(-1)^n ac(d^{r+n})$, since $ac$ is additive. Thus the definition extends to complexes up to quasi-isomorphism with precisely the claimed shift compatibility, without boundedness assumptions.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; shift convention as in the statement of lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization
